lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

Year on year it is still a headwind: the H1 2026 average was 3.03 NIS/USD against 3.6, and the Q3 2025 average was 3.36.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The currency was cited as the drag in the Q1 2026 release (-9.7%) and offset in Q2 (+3.5%); never the stated driver of a move on its own.

findings.finding: Elbit Systems, Israel's largest defense prime, reported Q3 2026 revenue up 17.2% to $2.25bn and backlog of $33.0bn (from $32bn in June) on 17 Nov. It guided to high-teens revenue growth in 2027. This fits continued Israeli defense-manufacturing demand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of BOSC reacting to a defense peer's print.

findings.finding: M&A: on the Q2 call (20 Aug) management said it was in negotiations with several targets (EBITDA multiple 5-6x, up to $20m with about 50% bank financing), with $2.9m of exercise proceeds earmarked. An accretive deal could be announced with the results.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No acquisition announcements in the reaction history.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin has not been the stated driver of a print move.

findings.finding: HMR rose +57% in four sessions into the print, from a 0.93 close on 11-23 to 1.46 on 11-27, and +44.6% over 5 days. Tanker peers rose +3.5% (NAT) and +5.3% (FRO) over the same days. Volume was 574k shares on the 11-27 half session against a 211k 20-day average, on a 6.04m-share float. No company release, filing or news explains it (the last release was 11-11, the last EDGAR filing 2026-09-09). The market has bid a large part of any good print in advance, which raises the real bar well above the $0.04 / $22m consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: the stock ran +29% on 2026-05-22 (1.16 to 1.50) before the 05-26 print, rose +4.7% on the print day, then fell -20.4% on 05-27. Q2 2026 came after no run-up and still fell -10.8% on a revenue beat. Bars: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/HMR?range=1y&interval=1d

findings.finding: MR product-tanker spot earnings roughly halved from Q2 to Q3 2026. Ardmore's MR spot TCE was $27,031/day in Q3 against $51,870 in Q2 (-48%), reported 2026-11-03, after HMR last spoke on 09-01. HMR runs an MR pool, so its MR pool fees for Q3 fall with that rate. The consensus of $21.5-22.4m against Q2's $29.0m already assumes about a 24% sequential revenue drop.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HMR does not disclose pool TCEs or segment fees, so no reaction to this line has been observed.

findings.finding: Suezmax Q3 2026 rates are mixed across peers. NAT had about 75% of Q3 days booked at about $54,000/day against a $63,000 Q2 TCE (-14%), per its 2026-08-31 report. Okeanis is reported by a secondary source at a Q3 Suezmax spot of $166,600/day (MEG-exposed, unverified against the company's release). HMR's Suezmax pool received 4 additional Suezmaxes in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not disclosed by HMR; none observed.

findings.finding: HMR's Q4 outlook commentary will describe October 2026, when crude tanker rates hit records. DHT had Q4 VLCC spot about 50% booked at $509,100/day as of 10-12, against a Q3 spot of $167,100. Okeanis Q4 Suezmax is booked at about $410,900/day (secondary). Ardmore's Q4 MR is booked at $57,600/day, against Q3's $27,031. HMR's pool fees scale with these rates, so a bullish Q4 statement is likely. Rates then corrected in November (Kpler 11-13: TD20 Suezmax -$3.14 to $7.86/bbl).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 09-01 management said rates would stay elevated into Q4/Q1, and the stock still fell -10.8%. Qualitative outlook has not bought this stock on the print day.

findings.finding: The revenue bar is low against HMR's own last print. Q3 consensus is $21.5m (Chartmill) to $22.4m against Q2's actual $29.0m, and Q2 itself beat $24.43m by 19%. The managed fleet grew afterwards: +7 commercially managed vessels in Q2, 3 more takeovers expected in Q3, and Q-Shipping (9 vessels, technical management) consolidated from 2026-07-01. A revenue beat is more likely than not, despite lower MR and Suezmax rates.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 revenue beat of +19% was sold for -10.8% because EPS missed. The EPS bar of $0.04 now equals Q2's actual, so it is a lower EPS hurdle than Q2's $0.10.
